specs.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/README.md §0.4 'Chips' and 'Workspace tags'; 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' #sys 'Chips — three kinds, three shapes' block; operator ruling 2.5
notes: Chips.tsx is pure inline style (media queries only affect <768px, not this 1440 mount); every property here is a real product value.

Ruling 2.5 restates the family rules (band = tinted pill + round dot; workspace tag = square dot, removable; kind/mode/topic = neutral, no dot, no border; tier = the only bordered chip) without new numbers for band/tier/tag beyond what the artboard states, so the artboard markup is the numeric source for those three.

TagChip has no `border` set at all (correct per ruling 2.5's 'no dot, NO border'); the artboard's neutral tag also has no border rule. Both sides agree, not asserted as a property since 'unset' has no single canonical getComputedStyle form worth comparing.

CONFIRMED, verified not a harness artefact: `--radius-pill` computes to nothing (CSSOM initial value, 0) in the real product, not just this harness. src/app/theme.css declares it TWICE inside the SAME plain `:root{}` rule (no `@theme` involved, no Tailwind step in play): line 55 `--radius-pill: 999px;`, then line 201 `--radius-pill: var(--radius-pill);` — a property declared in terms of itself, which CSS defines as invalid, and the invalid LATER declaration wins over the valid earlier one within one rule (there is no 'fall back to the earlier declaration' in CSS custom properties). Every chip that reads `var(--radius-pill)` — BandChip, WorkspaceTagPill, and TagChip (see next note) — renders SQUARE corners everywhere in the shipped product, not just in this measurement. Confirmed by probing `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--radius-pill')` directly against theme.css alone (empty string) before writing this spec.

TagChip's radius is a second, separate issue on top of the broken token: even if `--radius-pill` were fixed to 999px, the artboard's neutral tag uses `border-radius:4px` (a squared tag, matching the tier chip's own 4px-square convention), not a pill — TagChip.tsx reaches for the pill token where the design wants the square one.

FIXED by fix58-tokens (2026-09-07): removed theme.css's self-referential `--radius-pill: var(--radius-pill);` redeclaration (it carried no independent value and only broke the earlier valid one); `--radius-pill` now resolves to 999px sitewide. TagChip.tsx also switched to `border-radius:4px` (the design's square-tag value, not the pill token).

children.note: FOLD 60, and the reason this row is geometric rather than a bounds check. The date cell is `white-space: nowrap` in what was a HARD 70px track; 'Thu Sep 10' measures 75.7px, and every box up to the card is `overflow: visible`, so the date did not clip, its glyphs PAINTED 6px into the producer-name column beside it. A boundsCheck was written first and REFUTED BY ATTACK: restoring the hard 70px left it MATCH, because a bounds check compares element RECTS and the span's rect stays 70px while its text paints outside it. Text overflow is invisible to rect geometry. What does catch it is the resolved track list. The track is `minmax(70px, auto)`: row 1's single-digit date ('Sat Sep 5') still resolves to EXACTLY the artboard's 70px, and only row 2's two-digit date grows, by the 5.7px it actually needs, with the name column at `minmax(0, 1fr)` yielding them. notes: Region-composition check for the full page: AppShell (Sidebar + TopBar) + Masthead + MapPageView, all real components, mounted with populated fixture data via .discipline/rendering/audit/mounts.mjs['compose-map'] — no live Supabase project reachable in this sandbox (DEVIATION-LOG.md).

Artboard order top to bottom: Masthead (VOL line, REGULATORY MAP title, dek, page-scoped command bar) -> Mode/Band/Region filter row (ABOVE the map, not beside it — operator audit item, closed) -> Regulatory map card (map canvas + in-card KEY legend) -> Jurisdiction register card (table: JURISDICTION / ACTIVE THEMES / HIGHEST BAND / ITEMS, one ListRow per jurisdiction) -> Immediate strip foot -> rail: Immediate jurisdictions card, Coverage gaps card, Legend card, in that order alongside the two left-column cards (not below them).

Command bar placeholder is page-scoped: 'Search a jurisdiction — or ask "where are my immediate items?"' (dc.html p10 exact text) — this lane added the missing `placeholder` prop to src/app/map/page.tsx's Masthead call; before this lane it fell back to the generic 'Search or ask across N items…' copy.

The KEY box's fixture rows are limited to the mount's fixture data (6 resources across 4 jurisdictions) — the artboard shows 7 jurisdictions / 976 items from example data, never shipped (README: sample data in the mock is never shipped).

LANE map60 (2026-09-08), the four items from addendum 86 postscript 14's fold report on this artboard. (a) THE EMPTY CANVAS WAS THE FIXTURE, not the product [CONFIRMED by DOM measurement]: the mount aliases `leaflet/dist/leaflet.css` to an empty module so esbuild needs no output path for it, and nothing put the real stylesheet back, so Leaflet's four markers were built with correct transforms but laid out in normal flow ~2700px below the card. mounts.mjs now carries `styleFiles` and both run-audit.mjs and capture-compose-page.mjs inject it, the same technique ../smoke/map-smoke.mjs already used. leaflet is an existing app dependency; no external dependency and no network is added. (b) MODE and BAND now share the first line, REGION the second, because the filter row is `grid-column:1/-1` in the content grid at `gap:10px` with `flex-wrap:wrap`, as dc.html p10 has it. (c) The register carries p10's own column headers and per-row arrow through ListRowColumnHeader/ListRow's additive `variant="register"`. (d) The KEY's four band entries read '<Band> present' on uniform 8px dots.

NO BASEMAP TILES in this mount, and none in any sandbox capture: the tile layer is api-external (tile.openstreetmap.org) and every request fails with ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED behind the egress proxy. That is the environment, not the page, the artboard itself draws a hatched placeholder captioned 'BASEMAP · light, desaturated, no labels below country level' rather than a real basemap. No static fallback exists in the app and none was added (a new tile asset would be a new external dependency). Logged in DEVIATION-LOG.md.

CSS VARIABLES DO NOT RESOLVE in this mount (the compose-* mounts carry no STYLE_INJECT; capture-compose-page.mjs injects the compiled CSS for SCREENSHOTS only), so every `var(--fs-*)`/`var(--ink*)` value reads as the browser initial. The rows below therefore assert GEOMETRY (grid tracks, heights, padding, span widths) and TEXT, never token-derived colour or type, those are asserted on the token-styled mounts (map-register.json, listrow.json).

The fold keeps both mechanisms, so the page is now measured as the product actually renders it, with a 764px content column (the same value lane settings60 measured independently). 764 + 28 gap + 300 rail = 1092. The assertion is unchanged in kind and strength, exact equality on the same property; only the container it resolves against is now the real one.

notes: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (fold 60). The `compose-signup` mount was built, is maintained, and was measured by NOTHING. compose-16-auth.json's own title reads '/login, /signup' but its `mount` is `compose-signup`'s sibling `compose-login`, and no other spec named it, so the fold's mechanical mount/spec bijection check found it as the one AUDIT_MOUNTS entry with no spec. SITEWIDE FINDING, confirmed live (not a harness artefact): both filter-chip border-radius checks below measure 0px against theme.css's own --radius-pill:999px token. Root cause, confirmed by reading src/app/theme.css line 213: `--radius-pill: var(--radius-pill);` — a CUSTOM PROPERTY THAT REFERENCES ITSELF inside the same :root block that first declares `--radius-pill: 999px` at line 55. Per the CSS custom-properties spec, a property whose computed value cycles back to itself is 'guaranteed-invalid' and resolves to nothing wherever it is USED (there is no fallback in the `var(--radius-pill)` calls that consume it) — a definition-order bug, not a consumer bug. This is not scoped to FilterChip: every pill-radius shared part that reads `var(--radius-pill)` (BandChip, TagChip, WorkspaceTagPill, FilterChip — all in Chips.tsx) renders a SQUARE corner sitewide instead of the design's pill. Confirmed by a standalone debug mount reading `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--radius-pill')` against the real theme.css + globals.css bundle: returns the empty string. This lane writes no product code (dispatch: 'NO product code is written by this lane'); the fix (delete the redundant redeclaration at line 213, or point it at a differently-named canonical token) belongs to a product lane, flagged here with its exact line and mechanism per CLAUDE.md rule 13 ('a flag is a commitment'). artboards: 10-map (desktop); mobile-390 text spec (no 390 artboard PNG exists yet)
specs.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/DEVIATION-LOG.md 'MOBILE 390 SPEC', sections BREAKPOINTS ('below 1280: rail folds under the content') and MASTHEAD; operator mobile report 2026-09-08, D-M3.
notes: THE SPEC THIS LANE ADDS (mobfix61, 2026-09-08). The map page was the one surface with no 390 spec at all, and it was the surface the operator's own screenshot showed worst: its rail cards were drawn ON TOP of the MODE / BAND / REGION chip rows.

[CONFIRMED root cause, twice over] MapPageView.tsx's outer div is the two-column grid (`minmax(0,1fr) 300px`, className `cl-map-outer`), and the file's only media query named `.cl-map-grid` — the INNER content column, which is a `display: flex` element on which `grid-template-columns` does nothing at all. So the rule was dead twice over and the 300px rail track survived at every width. Nothing in the toolchain could see it: a CSS selector matching no element is not an error in any language involved. Nav card top margin is expected at 20px per operator ruling 4.2 ('margin: 20px 0 16px 16px so it aligns with the content column's 20px top padding. Fix it in the frame, once'). The artboard markup still shows 16px; the ruling supersedes it.

Ruling 5.1 requires a 3px graduated rule ABOVE each section title (full card width, top edge, no radius, linear-gradient(90deg,#5A5552,#5A5552 22%,rgba(90,85,82,.18))) and NO line below the title. This spec therefore checks the ONE permitted instance exactly (the nav card cap) and forbids a band-proportion rule inside a page masthead. Adding `data-band-rule` to BandGradientRule would make the sitewide count a one-line check; that is a recommendation for the fix lane, not a deviation.

Operator report 2026-09-07 ('the side navigation bar does not reach the length of the page'), CONFIRMED against every page artboard: the nav card is `align-self:stretch` inside the frame's `grid-template-columns:252px 1fr` and spans the full page height, footer rows at its foot. The build's `aside` previously carried `maxHeight: calc(100vh - 36px)` with no `align-self` of its own and ended at its content height instead. Fixed at the root in `Sidebar.tsx` (`align-self:stretch`, `height:auto`, no `maxHeight`) and in `AppShell.tsx` (the frame row's `display:flex`/height made inline, not Tailwind-class-only, so this harness — which injects only globals.css/theme.css, no compiled Tailwind CSS — has a real box to stretch against). The two rows below assert it: `align-self` reads back `stretch`, and `height` on this fixture (frame row's inline `height:100vh` at the harness's fixed 1400px page height) resolves to the frame height (1400px) minus the card's own vertical margins (20px top + 16px bottom = 36px) minus its own 1px top+bottom border (`box-sizing:content-box`, so the CSS `height` property excludes it) = 1362px — i.e. the card's rendered (border) box is exactly 1364px, equal to the frame's box, not its own content's height; the 1362px this row asserts is that same box read back through `getComputedStyle`'s content-box `height`, confirmed against `getBoundingClientRect().height === 1364` directly in the fixture.

notes: Sidebar.tsx's desktop nav card mixes inline style with Tailwind utility classes (`text-xl uppercase`, `text-[10px] font-bold tracking-[0.15em] uppercase`, etc. on the title/tagline). This harness injects `globals.css`/`theme.css` as RAW text without running Tailwind's build step (no PostCSS/Vite plugin — see mounts.mjs's STYLE_INJECT), so Tailwind's `@import "tailwindcss"` and its generated utility classes never resolve in this measured tree: a Tailwind-only property (e.g. the title's `text-xl` font-size) reads back as the browser's un-styled default, which is a HARNESS LIMITATION, not a product value — confirmed empirically (probed `aside.hidden > div:nth-child(2) h1` font-size: read 32px, the UA default h1 size, and text-transform: none, neither of which Sidebar.tsx's own inline style sets). This spec therefore asserts ONLY properties Sidebar.tsx sets via inline `style={}`, which bypass Tailwind entirely and are real regardless of this harness's raw-injection limitation. Title/tagline font-size, weight and text-transform (all Tailwind-class-driven in the desktop card) are NOT asserted here for that reason, not because they are known-correct.

The aside's own box model (width 252, margin, background, border, radius, band-gradient cap) is already covered by spec/page-frame.json's own top-level target on this same mount/selector; this spec adds the nav card's INTERNAL typography and active-state treatment, which page-frame.json does not touch.

specs.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' #sys 'Actions · stat block' (the ☆ Watch action button chrome: padding 8px 14px, border rgba(0,0,0,.25), radius 6, background #fff, font-size 12.5px, weight 600 — the family WatchButton.tsx's own header comment says the row variant matches: 'chrome matching ActionRow's other three buttons'); operator ruling 3.5 ('watched rows show a filled ★ in ink and the label "Watching"; the action on hover/menu is "Unwatch". A watched row must never read "Watch"'); src/components/ui/WatchButton.tsx (real component, mounted with `initialWatched` so no network fetch is needed to reach a deterministic watched/unwatched state)
notes: CONFIRMED live: WatchButton's row variant (RowWatchButton) satisfies ruling 3.5's FIRST half exactly — watched=true renders '★' (filled, aria-hidden) plus the literal label 'Watching', in ink (--ink, via ActionButton's secondary-variant colour); watched=false renders '☆' plus 'Watch'. Checked below.

Text checks below read '★Watching' / '☆Watch' with no space — RowWatchButton's glyph and label are adjacent JSX children with no whitespace text node between them, so textContent concatenates with none; this is the DOM's actual (harmless, whitespace-collapse-safe) concatenation, not a design statement about spacing, and matching it exactly avoids a false MISMATCH the harness's own README warns against (rule 14).

CONFIRMED ABSENT, by a codebase-wide grep ('grep -rn "Unwatch" src/'), zero matches: ruling 3.5's SECOND half ('the action on hover/menu is "Unwatch"') has no implementation anywhere in the product. RowWatchButton's label is `{watched ? "Watching" : "Watch"}` with no third, hover-only state — the control has no hover-driven text swap at all, so there is no element a selector could address for an 'Unwatch' string; this is stated in prose rather than forced into a spurious selector check, per this harness's own rule (a false MISMATCH is worse than no audit, CLAUDE.md rule 14). The gap is real and is the second half of the same ruling the row-label check below confirms the first half of.

rows.note: An unscored row's impact cell must render ImpactMeter's dashed baseline + Absence reason, never a fabricated zero score. The regex form is deliberate: a plain "0/12" substring also matches the legitimate "10/12", which made this forbid report a passing product as a defect.

rows.target: D-M4: no list row carries more than one absence token
rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third on a line of its own. Ruling 2.1 allows exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.target: region 7a, NEXT DATA DROPS row 1, a single-digit date keeps the artboard's exact 70px track
rows.note: FOLD 60, and the reason this row is geometric rather than a bounds check. The date cell is `white-space: nowrap` in what was a HARD 70px track; 'Thu Sep 10' measures 75.7px, and every box up to the card is `overflow: visible`, so the date did not clip, its glyphs PAINTED 6px into the producer-name column beside it. A boundsCheck was written first and REFUTED BY ATTACK: restoring the hard 70px left it MATCH, because a bounds check compares element RECTS and the span's rect stays 70px while its text paints outside it. Text overflow is invisible to rect geometry. What does catch it is the resolved track list. The track is `minmax(70px, auto)`: row 1's single-digit date ('Sat Sep 5') still resolves to EXACTLY the artboard's 70px, and only row 2's two-digit date grows, by the 5.7px it actually needs, with the name column at `minmax(0, 1fr)` yielding them. Reverting to `70px 1fr` turns this row MISMATCH (measured 70px 186px).

rows.target: D-M4: no list row carries more than one absence token
rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third on a line of its own. Ruling 2.1 allows exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.target: D-M4: no list row carries more than one absence token
rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third on a line of its own. Ruling 2.1 allows exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.target: region 2a, filter row spans the full content grid (grid-column 1/-1), one flex row, 10px gap
rows.note: dc.html p10: `grid-column:1/-1;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;padding:0 4px`. 1036px is the CONTENT-box width getComputedStyle reports for the full grid span in this mount (border box 1044 = content column 716 + 28 gap + 300 rail, less the 2x4px padding); the pre-map60 row sat INSIDE the content column and measured 716. FOLD 60 RECALIBRATION: this mount declares BOTH `needsCompiledCss` and `styleFiles`, but neither lane's harness read both. map60's run-audit.mjs had no `needsCompiledCss` reader (admin60 wrote it) and admin60's had no `mountExtraCss` reader (map60 wrote it), so map60 calibrated these values against a render with leaflet's stylesheet and NO app stylesheet: every `var(--fs-*)` fell back to 16px and the content column measured 716px. The fold keeps both mechanisms, so the page is now measured as the product actually renders it, with a 764px content column (the same value lane settings60 measured independently). 764 + 28 gap + 300 rail = 1092. The assertion is unchanged in kind and strength, exact equality on the same property; only the container it resolves against is now the real one.

The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third on a line of its own. rows.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' #sys: the list-row example's impact cell (row variant, scored + unscored) and the 'Impact meter — full' block; README.md §0.4 'Meters and timeline on every row'
rows.target: row unscored — the meter renders the dashed baseline and NO reason of its own (D-M4)
rows.note: UPDATED (lane mobfix61, 2026-09-08, operator mobile report D-M4). This asserted the meter's own text was "unscored". It was: the meter named the state itself while the row's due and tier cells named their own absences beside it, so one unscored row rendered three tokens — a dashed baseline, then UNSCORED, then PENDING, then NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE on a line of its own, which is what the operator photographed on 2026-09-08. Ruling 2.1 forbids the literal outright and allows exactly ONE reason per row. The meter no longer names a reason; the composite hands it one through `reason`, chosen by Absence.tsx's ABSENCE_PRECEDENCE. A spec pinning the old literal would be preserving the defect, so it asserts the unscored container instead, and the one-token invariant is asserted where it belongs, on the ROW (listrow.json / the mobile-* specs' `.cl-list-row .cl-absence` count).

rows.target: D-M4: no list row carries more than one absence token
rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third on a line of its own. Ruling 2.1 allows exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third wrapping onto a line of its own at 390 beside a dangling divider. Ruling 2.1 and the mobile 390 spec both allow exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else; a document-wide count cannot express "per row" and would read 16 on a 16-row surface that is entirely correct. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.target: D-M4: no list row carries more than one absence token
rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third wrapping onto a line of its own at 390 beside a dangling divider. Ruling 2.1 and the mobile 390 spec both allow exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else; a document-wide count cannot express "per row" and would read 16 on a 16-row surface that is entirely correct. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third wrapping onto a line of its own at 390 beside a dangling divider. Ruling 2.1 and the mobile 390 spec both allow exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else; a document-wide count cannot express "per row" and would read 16 on a 16-row surface that is entirely correct. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.target: D-M4: no list row carries more than one absence token
rows.note: D-M4 (operator mobile report 2026-09-08) [CONFIRMED at 1440 and at 390]. The impact, due and tier cells each rendered their own <Absence>, so a row missing all three drew a dashed baseline plus UNSCORED plus PENDING plus NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE — three tokens, the third wrapping onto a line of its own at 390 beside a dangling divider. Ruling 2.1 and the mobile 390 spec both allow exactly ONE reason per row. This selector matches a row carrying a token in TWO of the three cells, which is the defect and nothing else; a document-wide count cannot express "per row" and would read 16 on a 16-row surface that is entirely correct. The structural guarantee is ListRow's `reasonSlot`.

rows.target: exactly one '+ Tag' trigger in the detail header (operator 3.2, mechanism repair train 58 2026-09-07)
rows.note: Operator 3.2: 'The action-row + Tag is the only trigger. Applied workspace tags still render as a row under the title; that row displays tags, it does not carry the trigger.' RESOLVED (found and fixed independently by two fix lanes, fix58-tokens and fix58-detail, 2026-09-07): the count-5 finding was a HARNESS bug, not a product defect. A standalone debug mount (`page.evaluate` against this exact selector, no `textMatch` filter applied) confirmed `header:not(.cl-masthead) button` matches all 5 ActionRow buttons (the row-overflow '⋯' menu, Export brief, Share, ☆ Watch, + Tag) — `textMatch: "Tag"` above was meant to narrow that down to the one button whose text contains 'Tag', exactly the way `forbid` entries already use `textMatch` (readForbid, run-audit.mjs). But `targetsOf()`/`readTarget()` (the non-forbid path) silently dropped the `textMatch` field for `children`/top-level `expect` targets — it was read into the target object nowhere, so the filter never ran and the raw 5-button count leaked through. Fixed at the root, once, in run-audit.mjs (`targetsOf` now carries `textMatch` through, `readTarget` applies the same filter `readForbid` already does) rather than reshaping this selector around the bug. RegulationDetailSurface.tsx (line ~193, ~209) already wires exactly one '+ Tag' trigger (ActionRow's own, via `onTag`) and DetailTagRow renders no trigger of its own (TagPopover's `open`/`onOpenChange` controlled mode) — the product was already correct; only the measurement was wrong.
